tools.name: advance_outcome

Before the run: brief (the pinned-down outcome), plan (research and the composed plan, checked against our rules and the live catalogue), approve_plan (owner only). During the run: data, start, complete (with outputs and checks), approve (owner only), skip, block, r

tools.name: record_outcome_decision
tools.description: Record what the owner chose, the options considered (best-ranked first), what they passed over and why. Passing over the top option needs a reason. Returns a line for decisions.jsonl and, if a durable rule was stated, a learning candidate with where to save it.

tools.name: record_outcome_experiment

tools.name: read_back_outcome_experiment

With a reading: compares it with the registered baseline, minimum volume and guardrails; flags a guardrail breach at on

tools.name: prepare_outcome_pattern
tools.description: After a finished round, returns the exact anonymised PATTERN.json the owner would share (names, figures, links and contact details removed) and its sha256. Only if the owner says yes to that file, call again with consent to get PATTERN-SUBMISSION.json for review by a person at AI Blocks. Nothing is

tools.name: prepare_job_context
tools.description: The first call for any piece of work: a page, ad, email, copy, audit, analysis, plan or code. Returns a short brief to act on, up to 3 questions to ask (each with a default) and whether one lead or a team fits. Also an annex to save: what to capture from the client’s real site or data, the rubric an

tools.name: start_job
tools.description: Decides who does a job and says why. One kind of work: one lead, with the lead to load, the questions and the rubric. Mixed kinds of work, a large batch or mode team: one lead with helpers, the short team method and a state for advance_job. All work runs in the user’s AI; no server model calls or ac

tools.name: advance_job
tools.description: Team jobs only. Send the latest complete state and state_digest unchanged, with one event and its document. Each step checks its record; a refusal names the field to fix. Artifacts stay local; send hashes. Every result is a host report, not proof of execution or consent.

tools.name: propose_team
tools.description: The roster a team job would get: one lead who owns the deliverable and the helpers it may call, matched from published roles and personas. start_job returns this for a team job. Review any unmapped catalogue gaps before accepting.

tools.name: get_approaches
tools.description: Read source-backed approach families, methods, lenses and needed tools. Coverage and review gaps are reported honestly. Pass job or task.

tools.name: get_job_templates
tools.description: JOB-METHOD.md (the short team method), JOB-RECORDS.md (every record field; open it only when advance_job refuses a record) and the delivery templates.

tools.name: get_job_preferences
tools.description: On this anonymous service, return recommended choices and a local-file template. Signed-in connections use the scoped private preference record. No private data is loaded publicly.

tools.name: set_job_preferences
tools.description: Anonymous calls only prepare local preference files; they save nothing on the server. Signed-in connections require the selected workspace write consent. An ordinary one-off request never changes saved defaults.

tools.name: find_specialist
tools.description: Find worker candidates for a deliverable. Compare their remit and outputs, then use prepare_specialist to onboard the chosen worker. Keep unrelated private context out of discovery.

tools.name: prepare_specialist
tools.description: Supply role_id only to load a complete base specialist: README, setup, SOUL, intake, playbook, handoff and best-practice files, pinned methods and a full ZIP download. The host AI asks task and output questions in the conversation; no website context form is required. Optionally include task and rel

tools.description: Look up one item (to start a piece of work, use prepare_job_context; for a business goal, start_outcome). Find skills, workflows, agents, prompts, minds, AI tools and mini tools by keywords and intent. Filters: type, job, level, tested, since (what's new). With no query, a job or since browses. Retu

Before calling, form a task brief from the current chat, supplied files and authorized me.md (get_me when available): outcomes, formats, audience, constraints, available inputs and checks. Keep p

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Retrieve a skill. Concise (default): summary, inputs, outputs, how to use, file list with hashes, and step_map (what usually goes before and after it and the input each passes on). response_format detailed adds the full SKILL.md instructions and resource links; use it before running the skill. Pin r

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Retrieve a public workflow, its declared order and skill references, plus handoff_check: which step passes each input to which, and which inputs the user gives. Returns a diagram you can show the user (Mermaid; detailed adds a text outline) and open_in_builder, a link that opens it in the site's bui

tools.name: get_resource
tools.description: Read one inventoried resource at an exact skill revision. Text returns bounded ordered chunks; follow next_offset until null and verify full character coverage. Binary files return a download descriptor for the host to retrieve and verify. Paths are archive-relative, never arbitrary URLs or filesyst

tools.name: prepare_workflow
tools.description: Check a workflow, or a change to one. Call it whenever the user wants to see, check or change a workflow (swap, add, remove or reorder steps), and before showing any plan. Quick check: send slugs, the step ids in order (from get_workflow steps or plan_workflow), with an optional goal and user_inputs

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Get one item of any kind by the id from search_library: an agent, prompt, mind, AI tool or mini tool (skills and workflows work too). Concise (default): what it does, inputs and outputs, how to use it, files or links, and for AI tools the price, limits and when we last checked. response_format detai

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search AI Blocks in the shape ChatGPT deep research and company knowledge use: results with id, title and url. Read one with fetch. search_library does the same with filters and one-line summaries.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Read one item by the id from search (such as skill/ad-angle-planner): its full text (the SKILL.md, or the AI tool or mini tool record), url to cite and metadata. Text over 48,000 characters is cut; metadata.rest says how to read the rest.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "plan_workflow" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Find candidate steps for a multi-step job; these are suggestions, not a complete context-validated plan. Before calling, form a task brief from the current chat…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: prepare_outcome_pattern, propose_team, get_approaches, search_library, plan_workflow, get_resource, prepare_workflow, get_item, search, fetch · Private data: start_outcome, record_outcome_decision, record_outcome_experiment, prepare_outcome_pattern, advance_job, get_job_templates, get_job_preferences, set_job_preferences, find_specialist, prepare_specialist, plan_workflow, get_skill, get_resource, get_item, fetch · Public sink: record_outcome_experiment, prepare_outcome_pattern, prepare_job_context, advance_job, plan_workflow, prepare_workflow · Destructive: start_outcome, advance_outcome, get_workflow, prepare_workflow.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: prepare_outcome_pattern, propose_team, get_approaches, search_library, plan_workflow, get_resource, prepare_workflow, get_item, search, fetch · Private data: start_outcome, record_outcome_decision, record_outcome_experiment, prepare_outcome_pattern, advance_job, get_job_templates, get_job_preferences, set_job_preferences, find_specialist, prepare_specialist, plan_workflow, get_skill, get_resource, get_item, fetch · Public sink: record_outcome_experiment, prepare_outcome_pattern, prepare_job_context, advance_job, plan_workflow, prepare_workflow · Destructive: start_outcome, advance_outcome, get_workflow, prepare_workflow

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "start_outcome" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
